title: Tense and aspect for politeness and attitude

objective.en: Use past forms to sound tentative, continuous forms with always to sound irritated, and will have to make confident assumptions about the present.
objective.fr: Utiliser le passé pour paraître hésitant, le continu avec always pour montrer l'agacement, et will have pour faire des suppositions sur le présent.
objective.de: Vergangenheitsformen für zurückhaltende Bitten, Continuous-Formen mit always für Ärger und will have für Vermutungen über die Gegenwart verwenden.

instructions.en: Read the explanation and the examples.

heading.en: The past as a polite step back
heading.fr: Le passé comme pas en arrière poli
heading.de: Die Vergangenheit als höflicher Schritt zurück

text.en:
To sound **tentative**, English steps back into the past. The past does not mean past time here: it adds distance and makes a request easier to refuse.

- `I hope you can help.` becomes `I was hoping you could help.`
- `I want to ask something.` becomes `I wanted to ask something.`
- The past continuous (`was hoping`, `was wondering`) is softer than the past simple.

Add `could` or `would` in the second part: `I was wondering if you could...`
text.fr:
Pour paraître **hésitant** et poli, l'anglais recule dans le passé. Ce passé n'exprime pas le temps : il crée de la distance et rend une demande plus facile à refuser.

- `I hope you can help.` devient `I was hoping you could help.`
- `I want to ask something.` devient `I wanted to ask something.`
- Le past continuous (`was hoping`, `was wondering`) est plus doux que le prétérit simple.

Ajoutez `could` ou `would` dans la seconde partie : `I was wondering if you could...`
text.de:
Um **zurückhaltend** und höflich zu klingen, geht das Englische in die Vergangenheit zurück. Diese Vergangenheit meint keine Zeit: Sie schafft Abstand und macht eine Bitte leichter ablehnbar.

- `I hope you can help.` wird zu `I was hoping you could help.`
- `I want to ask something.` wird zu `I wanted to ask something.`
- Das Past Continuous (`was hoping`, `was wondering`) klingt weicher als das Simple Past.

Setze im zweiten Teil `could` oder `would` ein: `I was wondering if you could...`

label.en: Showing irritation with always and the continuous
label.fr: Montrer son agacement avec always et le continu
label.de: Ärger zeigen mit always und Continuous

instructions.en: Read the explanation and the examples.
instructions.de: Lies die Erklärung und die Beispiele.

text.en:
Use the present continuous with **always**, **constantly** or **forever** to show irritation at a repeated habit. The speaker means: this happens too often.

- `She's constantly losing her keys.`
- `He's always leaving the lights on.`
- `You were forever interrupting me.` (a past habit that annoyed you)

The simple present is neutral: `She loses her keys.` Tone and stress carry the complaint.
text.fr:
Employez le présent continu avec **always**, **constantly** ou **forever** pour montrer votre agacement devant une habitude qui se répète. Le sens : cela arrive trop souvent.

- `She's constantly losing her keys.`
- `He's always leaving the lights on.`
- `You were forever interrupting me.` (une habitude passée qui agaçait)

Le présent simple est neutre : `She loses her keys.` Le ton et l'accent portent le reproche.
text.de:
Benutze das Present Continuous mit **always**, **constantly** oder **forever**, um Ärger über eine wiederholte Gewohnheit zu zeigen. Gemeint ist: Das passiert zu oft.

- `She's constantly losing her keys.`
- `He's always leaving the lights on.`
- `You were forever interrupting me.` (eine vergangene Gewohnheit, die störte)

Das Simple Present ist neutral: `She loses her keys.` Ton und Betonung tragen den Vorwurf.

label.fr: Faire des suppositions avec will have

instructions.en: Read the explanation and the examples.
instructions.de: Lies die Erklärung und die Beispiele.

heading.fr: Deviner avec le futur antérieur anglais

text.en:
To make an **assumption** about the present, use `will have` plus a past participle, or `will have been` plus an -ing form for something that has been going on for a while.

- `You'll have been travelling all day.`
- `She'll have heard the news by now.`
- `You'll have had a long journey.`

The speaker is not predicting the future. They are guessing what is probably true now or has probably already happened.
text.fr:
Pour faire une **supposition** sur le présent, employez `will have` + participe passé, ou `will have been` + forme en -ing pour une action qui dure depuis un moment.

- `You'll have been travelling all day.`
- `She'll have heard the news by now.`
- `You'll have had a long journey.`

Le locuteur ne prédit pas l'avenir. Il devine ce qui est probablement vrai maintenant ou déjà arrivé.
text.de:
Für eine **Vermutung** über die Gegenwart nimmst du `will have` plus Partizip Perfekt, oder `will have been` plus -ing-Form für etwas, das schon eine Weile andauert.

- `You'll have been travelling all day.`
- `She'll have heard the news by now.`
- `You'll have had a long journey.`

Der Sprecher sagt nicht die Zukunft voraus. Er vermutet, was jetzt wahrscheinlich stimmt oder schon geschehen ist.
